newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian central bank to curb bank ADR issues.
newsitem.headline: Russian central bank to curb bank ADR issues.

text.p: Russia's central bank will minimise the amount of American or Global Depositary Receipts issued by banks, a senior bank official said on Tuesday.
ADRs and GDRs deprive the Russian securities market of capital, Dmitry Budakov, head of the department for control of bank activities on financial markets, told a news conference.
"We understand this is caused by certain economic problems in the country, including infrastructure underdevelopment," he said.
"It is difficult for corporations to attract foreign capital, besides, it is a question of prestige. But the central bank will take every step to minimise ADR issues by banks."
He said the central bank had set up a special department for new financial instruments, which was ordered to work out a control methodology for ADR issues.
"The work has just started as the central bank had not yet decided to which extent it wants to control the market," Budakov said.

The issue needs consideration as every transaction in Russian bank shares involving a foreign partner requires Russian central bank permission, while countries where ADRs are traded do not require such permission.
Inkombank, Bank Menatep and Bank Vozrozhdeniye have received permission from the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission to issue ADRs.
